name: CreditAccess Grameen Ltd
about: CreditAccess Grameen Limited is registered as a non-deposit accepting NBFC - Microfinance Institution with the RBI. It is engaged in providing microfinance services to women who are enrolled as members and organized as Joint Liability Groups. It also uses its distribution channel to provide certain other financial products and services to the members. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 19.7% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 42.8%.
Revenue growth accelerated from 8% to 26% YoY over the last 4 quarters.

cash.note: For lenders, operating cash flow mostly reflects loan-book growth; cash conversion isn't a meaningful test.

flags.text: Promoter holding down 2.5 pp in a year (66.4% → 63.8%)

ledger.quote: ROA of 5.2% to 5.8%
ledger.statement: Raised FY27 ROA guidance to 5.2-5.8% (from 4-4.8%)
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: H1 FY27 ROA 5.9% (C1) is above the top of the raised 5.2-5.8% range, which implies H2 ROA of roughly 4.5-5.7% as the 50 bps lending-rate cuts (G11) feed through. Raised from 4.0-4.8% (G25).

ledger.quote: ROE of 21% to 24%
ledger.statement: Raised FY27 ROE guidance to 21-24% (from 16-20%)
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: H1 FY27 ROE 23.8% (C1), inside the raised 21-24% range. F:roe_latest_pct of 11.0% looks like a trailing full-year figure and is not comparable; H1 PAT of INR 995 crore annualised on implied equity of ~INR 8,900 crore (borrowings / debt-to-equity) gives ~22%, consistent with the guide.

ledger.quote: We retain our AUM growth guidance of 20% to 25%
ledger.statement: FY27 AUM growth of 20-25%
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: AUM grew 19.5% YoY to INR 30,946 crore at Q2 FY27, just below the 20% floor, and only 2.1% QoQ (~9% annualised) (C1). Management concedes Group Loan growth is below guided levels and needs an H2 recovery (G7). Disbursements +19.4% YoY.
ledger.actual_text: AUM +19.5% YoY, +2.1% QoQ at Q2 FY27 (C1)

ledger.quote: We expect a NIM of 14.4% to 14.7%
ledger.statement: FY27 NIM of 14.4-14.7% (from 12.8-13.2% guided earlier)
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: No H1 NIM figure is in the inputs; management says current NIMs are at their highest levels (C2), above the 14.2% Q4 FY26 exit (C4). H2 absorbs 50 bps lending-rate cuts in Q3 and Q4 (G11) with borrowing cost guided flat at 9.2-9.3% (G9), so H2 NIM should run below H1.
ledger.actual_text: H1 FY27 NIM not in inputs; Q4 FY26 NIM 14.2% (C4)

ledger.quote: We're maintaining our credit cost guidance of 3% to 4%
ledger.statement: FY27 credit cost guidance of 3-4%
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: Management says credit cost is 'within the guided range' and has 'held its ground' (C2); no H1 credit-cost figure is in the inputs. The 3.5-4% steer given on the same call (G8) puts the outcome in the upper half of the range. Lowered from 4-4.5% guided in Q3 FY26 (G31).
ledger.actual_text: Not disclosed; within range per management (C2)

ledger.quote: Cost to income may range between 29% to 30%
ledger.statement: Cost-to-income ratio of 29-30% in FY27
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: Cut from 33-35% (G23). No H1 cost-to-income figure in the inputs; Q4 FY26 was 30.4% (C4). 60 branches added in Q2 (C1) add cost.
ledger.actual_text: Q4 FY26 30.4% (C4); H1 FY27 not disclosed

ledger.quote: we expect the Group Loan book growth to return to guided levels
ledger.statement: Group Loan book growth to return to guided levels in H2FY27
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: H2 FY27 not reported. The promise itself confirms Group Loan growth was below guided levels in H1; total AUM grew 2.1% QoQ in Q2 (C1).

ledger.quote: you should assume that it will be somewhere between 3.5% to 4%
ledger.statement: Credit cost likely between 3.5-4% for the year
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: A narrower steer inside the 3-4% headline (G5), at its upper half; management says credit cost is within the guided range (C2). No reported figure in the inputs.
ledger.actual_text: Not disclosed; within range per management (C2)

ledger.quote: our borrowing cost will stay in this 9.2% to 9.3% range till March
ledger.statement: Borrowing cost to stay at 9.2-9.3% until Mar-2027
ledger.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi
ledger.evidence: Reiterated in Q2 FY27: maturing debt is being refinanced at similar rates and an October USD 175m ECB replaces a costlier USD 200m ECB; balance-sheet blended rate ~9% (C3). Risks: repo rates have risen (C2), ~30% of borrowings are repo-linked and Q3 marginal cost will be higher (C3).

ledger.quote: our targeted ROA of 4.5% to 5% on a steady-state basis
ledger.statement: Targeted steady-state ROA of 4.5-5%
ledger.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi
ledger.evidence: Steady-state target with no date. H1 FY27 ROA of 5.9% (C1) and the FY27 guide of 5.2-5.8% (G1) are both above it, so management is signalling that current returns exceed what it considers sustainable, implying a 90-140 bps step-down from H1 levels at some point.

ledger.quote: we will pass on 50 bps in third quarter, fourth quarter and next year's Q1
ledger.statement: Lending rate cuts of 50 bps each in Q3FY27, Q4FY27 and Q1FY28
ledger.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi
ledger.evidence: The first 50 bps cut falls in Q3 FY27, not yet reported. Management has already made the next cut conditional: if borrowing costs rise 'we have the right to reprice or not necessarily pass back the 50 bps' (C2), with repo rates up and ~30% of borrowings repo-linked (C3).

ledger.quote: Microfinance, as we said in our strategic plan, could be range bound in the range of anywhere between 10% to 12%.
ledger.statement: Microfinance growth range-bound at 10-12%
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: Management concedes Group Loan growth is below guided levels in H1 FY27 (G7); no microfinance growth figure is disclosed. The Q2 FY27 wording ('could be range bound... 10% to 12%') is softer than the 12% net MFI growth stated in Q4 FY26 (G28).

ledger.quote: we are looking at around 6% to 8% of our customers on a yearly basis getting converted into individual
ledger.statement: About 6-8% of customers per year to convert to individual loans
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: No customer-conversion data in the inputs.

ledger.quote: We remain fully committed to our medium-term guidance of INR 50,000 Crore AUM by calendar year 2028
ledger.statement: AUM of INR 50,000 crore by calendar 2028
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: From INR 30,946 crore at Sep-2026 (C1), reaching INR 50,000 crore by Dec-2028 needs ~24% annual growth over 27 months; at the current 19.5% YoY pace AUM would reach ~INR 46,200 crore, ~8% short.

ledger.quote: accordingly take a call on passing the pricing benefit to the customers in H2 FY27
ledger.statement: Decision on passing pricing benefit to customers in H2FY27, per pricing policy
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan

ledger.quote: by end of Q2 FY27, probably can look at a 50 bps price cut if we are able to hold the asset quality
ledger.statement: Possible 50 bps price cut by end Q2FY27, conditional on asset quality
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan

ledger.quote: It may end somewhere at 9.4% average, we may still hold around 9.3%

ledger.quote: the trailing 12-month credit cost will also drop below 4%

ledger.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi

ledger.quote: ensure that our cross-cycle returns are in the range of 4.5% and ROEs are around 18%-20%
ledger.statement: Cross-cycle ROE of 18-20% (ROA about 4.5%)
ledger.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi

ledger.quote: maybe we may have to take 50 bps pricing cut in third quarter, maybe another 50 bps in fourth quarter
ledger.statement: Possible 50 bps pricing cut in Q3FY27 and another 50 bps in Q4FY27, tied to credit cost
ledger.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi

ledger.quote: For FY27, we are guiding an AUM growth of 20.0-25.0%
ledger.statement: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 20-25%
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: Same target as G3, set in Q4 FY26 and retained in Q2 FY27; H1 tracking at 19.5% YoY with 2.1% QoQ growth in Q2 (C1), and Group Loan growth below guide (G7).

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management raised FY27 ROA, ROE and NIM guidance and says it is best placed to protect NIMs, while noting credit-cost and drought-related watch points.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management says "we remain fully committed to our medium-term guidance" and "Currently, we are much comfortable on the guidance front", while making pricing cuts conditional on credit cost.

tones.label: mixed
tones.why: Management reaffirms FY27 guidance and calls Q4 an inflection, but acknowledges a credit cost miss versus guidance and widens the credit-cost range to absorb macro uncertainty.

tones.label: cautious
tones.why: Management says asset quality is normalising, but repeatedly defers firm FY27 growth and credit cost guidance until it sees the trend hold into May.

context.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
context.text: Thank you, Abhijit. A very good evening, everyone, and a very warm welcome to discuss our second quarter and first half of FY27 business performance. We reported our highest quarterly profit of INR 502 Crore in this quarter, having grown fivefold over the past 5 years. Current financial year marks a clear turnaround, recording INR 995 Crore PAT in the first half as against INR 778 Crore PAT during the previous financial year. Our H1 ROA stood at 5.9% and ROE stood at 23.8%. We are delivering record profitability while remaining amongst the most competitively priced lenders across our product segments. Our lending franchise today spans across Group Loans, Individual Business Loans, secured business loans, affordable housing loans and 2-wheeler finance, with growth, margins and asset quality all moving in the right direction. Our AUM grew 19.5% YoY and 2.1% QoQ to INR 30,946 Crore. Disbursements stood at INR 6,355 Crore, up 19.4% YoY and 4.1% QoQ, taking H1 disbursements to INR 12,461 Crore. We added 2.3 Lakh new borrowers, of which 35% were new-to-credit, taking our H1 additions to 4.9 Lakh customers. We also opened 60 new branches during the quarter, expanding our network to 2,326 branches across 460 districts. Digital collections rose to 26.3% versus 18.1% a year ago. When we began building our retail franchise, our thesis was very simple. The customers we've served for years would need more than a Group Loan as their economic profile improves and financing needs expand. That thesis continues to play out at scale with regulatory support in place. Of the ~45 Lakh borrower base, 15% or 6.8 Lakh borrowers belong to Retail Finance. context.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
context.text: Renish, our current NIMs are at highest levels. And as you know, the lending rate is guided by our pricing policy, which takes into account several factors, including your credit cost, including your cost of borrowing as well as opex. Only lever today is if credit costs increase, that is when we can retain this pricing. Now the credit cost since we are publishing within the guided range and being driven by the pricing policy, this will be range bound. We have earlier also indicated we will do a 50-bps cut this quarter and probably 50-bps in the next quarter. The marginal cost of borrowing increase is slightly because of the mix of borrowing that we've taken right now and not necessarily indicating a higher increase point of time. We do acknowledge that the repo rates have gone up, but it will be gradually passed and that will go through. If, for example, if the cost of borrowing goes up in next quarter, we have the right to reprice or not necessarily pass back the 50 bps that is planned for the next quarter also. I think it is something that we work on. But at this point of time, we need to pass this 50 bps to the customer given that the credit cost has held its ground.

context.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi
context.text: Renish, Nilesh here. So I'll add a couple of points. So firstly, on the borrowing cost, we do have borrowings from a wide range of lenders. So there are more than 80 lending institutions. And obviously, the borrowing rates will be within the range. That's where the blended rate what appears on the balance sheet is around 9%. So in second quarter, obviously, we did a couple of NCD transactions. We had a couple of longer tenure funds, which obviously will come at a slightly higher rate. But at the same time, what we have to also look at is the loans what we are replacing. So like even in third quarter, we will see the marginal borrowing cost will be higher because we have done a USD 175 million ECB in month of October, which will come at a higher rate. But it will also replace the USD 200 million ECB, which is going to expire in the same month. And the new ECB what we have taken is at a lower rate compared to the previous ECB which is getting replaced. Now when I look at my borrowing for next 6 months, the amount what we are going to draw down at a similar rate of the amount what we are going to repay. So that's where we are of a view that our borrowing cost will stay in this 9.2% to 9.3% range till March. While we do have certain repo-linked exposures, but around 30% of our borrowings are fixed. 40% are linked to MCLR and balance 30% are linked to the loans which are linked to repo, they reprice at different points in time. So it is not that it will immediately kind of add to the corporate borrowing and the MCLR-linked borrowings, typically, they react with much lag. And today, given the liquidity in the system, we have seen instances in a couple of banks that the MCLR has even come down. So from that perspective, as of now, we have visibility on the borrowing cost. And

The proportion of digital collections increased YoY from 14% in Q4 FY25 to 22% in Q4 FY26. NIMs expanded by 35 bps QoQ to 14.2% in Q4. Cost of borrowing further declined to 9.2% in Q4, marking a total 60 bps reduction during the year. Our marginal cost of borrowing continued to remain around 8.9% in Q4. Liability diversification was on track with the share of foreign borrowings increasing from 21% to 24.4%. Cost-to-income ratio improved QoQ to 30.4%. PPOP grew 23.1% YoY and 14.7% QoQ to INR 780 Crore in Q4, while PAT grew over 6x YoY and 34.7% QoQ to INR 340 Crore, translating to an ROA of 4.4% and an ROE of 17.8%.

So, with no extraordinary event present, we should be in similar range, but we will have to come back to you in May.

business.what_it_does: Lender to low-income borrowers, built on microfinance Group Loans and extending into Individual Business Loans, secured business loans, affordable housing loans and two-wheeler finance as customers' needs grow (6-8% of customers a year expected to move to individual loans, G13). AUM INR 30,946 crore at Q2 FY27 across 2,326 branches in 460 districts (C1).

segments.name: Group Loans (microfinance)
segments.comment: Core product. Management concedes Group Loan growth is below guided levels in H1 FY27 and frames microfinance growth at 10-12% (G7, G12). Share of AUM not stated in inputs.

segments.name: Retail: individual business, secured business, affordable housing, two-wheeler loans
segments.comment: Growth engine fed by graduating Group Loan customers (C1, G13). Share of AUM not stated in inputs.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Record quarterly profit of INR 502 crore and 'a clear turnaround': H1 PAT INR 995 crore vs INR 778 crore for all of FY26 (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The numbers agree: Q2 PAT +298.4% YoY, margin 35.2% vs 11.2% a year earlier, TTM PAT INR 1,587 crore. But 3-year PAT CAGR is -2.0%, so TTM profit is still below its level three years ago; this is a recovery to prior earnings, not beyond them.
AUM +19.5% YoY and +2.1% QoQ at Q2 FY27 (C1); management concedes Group Loan growth is below guided levels (G7). The guide was held while the run-rate sits under its floor.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: H1 ROE of 23.8% supports raising FY27 ROE guidance to 21-24% (C1, G2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: F:roe_latest_pct shows 11.0%, but that appears to be a trailing full-year figure; H1 PAT of INR 995 crore annualised on implied equity of ~INR 8,900 crore (borrowings INR 25,128 crore / debt-to-equity 2.82) gives ~22%, inside the new range.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: NIM will hold at 14.4-14.7% for FY27 while passing on 50 bps lending-rate cuts in Q3 and Q4 (G4, G11), with borrowing cost flat at 9.2-9.3% (G9).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Margin already slipped from 37.0% in Q1 to 35.2% in Q2; repo rates have risen, ~30% of borrowings are repo-linked and Q3 marginal borrowing cost will be higher (C2, C3). Whether NIM holds through 100 bps of yield cuts is not yet visible.

bull.point: Earnings reset: Q2 PAT INR 502 crore (+298.4% YoY); H1 PAT of INR 995 crore already exceeds FY26's INR 778 crore; H1 ROA 5.9% / ROE 23.8% sit at or above the raised 5.2-5.8% / 21-24% guides.

Guidance has room: FY27 targets issued in Q4 FY26 sat below that quarter's actuals (NIM 12.8-13.2% vs 14.2%; cost-to-income 33-35% vs 30.4%) and have been raised to 14.4-14.7% and 29-30%; the credit-cost guide fell from 4-4.5% (Q3 FY26) to 3-4%.

Franchise still expanding: revenue growth accelerated 8.0%, 13.5%, 21.9%, 26.3% over four quarters; 4.9 lakh new borrowers in H1 (35% new-to-credit in Q2), 60 branches added to 2,326, digital collections 26.3% vs 18.1%; borrowing cost guided flat at 9.2-9.3% with 30% of borrowings fixed-rate.

bear.point: Peak returns: management's own steady-state ROA of 4.5-5% (G10) is 90-140 bps below H1's 5.9%, and three 50 bps lending-rate cuts start in Q3 (G11) just as repo rates rise and Q3 marginal borrowing cost goes up (C2, C3).
Book growth lags guidance: AUM +19.5% YoY and +2.1% QoQ vs 20-25% guided (G3); Group Loan growth below guide (G7); INR 50,000 crore by CY2028 (G14) needs ~24% a year from INR 30,946 crore.

Credit cost is the swing factor at 2.82x debt/equity (borrowings INR 25,128 crore): the 3.5-4% steer (G8) is the top half of the 3-4% guide (G5), and the last credit cycle left 3-year PAT CAGR at -2.0% and margin down 1,470 bps over three years.

questions: What were H1 FY27 annualised credit cost and monthly PAR 15 accretion against the 30-35 bps built into the Q3 FY26 guide (G31), and why steer to 3.5-4% (G8) when the headline guide is 3-4%?
What Q4 FY27 exit NIM does the 14.4-14.7% full-year guide assume after 100 bps of lending-rate cuts (G11), and why was the FY27 NIM guide cut to 12.8-13.2% in Q4 FY26 when that quarter printed 14.2%?
With AUM up only 2.1% QoQ in Q2, what Group Loan versus retail growth was achieved in H1, and what H2 disbursement run-rate is needed to reach 20% FY27 AUM growth and INR 50,000 crore by CY2028?
